The prototype at **http://maker:4001** now reflects all of that. It's the same calm layout — I've only changed the saving experience. Please try these **three actions in order**, and tell me your reaction to each:

**1) Save with a review step.** Paste a link and press **Add**. Instead of saving instantly, a small **review panel** appears with the gathered title (editable), a description box for you to fill in, and the site shown with its icon. Change the title to something you'd actually recognise, add a short description, then press **Save bookmark**. Watch it land at the top.

**2) Try saving the very same link again.** Paste that identical link and press **Add**. It should *not* make a second copy — instead it should jump you to the one you already saved (it'll glow briefly) and open it for updating.

**3) Edit one later.** On any saved card, press **Edit**, change the title or description, and **Save changes**.

Here are the choices I made that I'd especially like your reaction to:

- **I added that review step *before* saving** so you can correct the title and description in the moment. But you also told me you want to **save quickly** — so I want to check: does pausing on this review panel feel worth it, or does it get in the way of a fast save? (If it feels like friction, I have other ways we could arrange this.)

- **The site name is no longer a pill.** To keep it from looking like one of your own tags, I moved it to a **quiet line with the little icon** at the bottom of each card. Does that read clearly as "where this came from" rather than a tag?

- **Description starts empty** (with a faint prompt) rather than me inventing page text. In the real app it'd arrive pre-filled from the page — here I didn't want to show you fake content. Is an editable description in this spot what you pictured?
